api.slots.lede: Each one spreads over an inner element, so you can restyle a region without forking the component.

guides.index.lede: Every page in this section, in reading order.
home.closing.body: The core is MIT and public. Install it, theme it, and ship both platforms from the same components.
home.closing.title: Build the whole product from one catalogue
home.lede: Nebula is a UI library where the contract lives in the tokens and each platform only implements the visual layer. Two products that look nothing alike ship from the same components — you change the theme, never the code.
home.legal: Core released under the MIT licence. Domain packages are licensed commercially.
home.motion.body: Components read motion.tier from the theme instead of hardcoding durations. Set it to minimal and every loop, spring and reveal on this page stops — the same path prefers-reduced-motion takes.
home.motion.title: One switch retunes every animation
home.numbers.title: Measured, not claimed
home.pillar.a11y.body: Every story runs axe on every commit, alongside keyboard, reduced-motion, contrast and visual-regression gates. Eight of them, all blocking.
home.pillar.a11y.title: Accessibility is a gate, not a promise
home.pillar.budget.body: size-limit measures each entry point in brotli kB and fails the build when it drifts. Heavy dependencies live behind subpaths you opt into.
home.pillar.budget.title: Every module has a budget
home.pillar.theme.body: The NebulaTheme contract covers the whole visual surface, including the variant recipes. A product retunes all of it from one object.
home.pillar.theme.title: Colour, type, motion, radii, shadows, glass
home.pillars.title: What the theme actually reaches
home.preview.tooltip: The scene is gradients over theme vars, so it retints too
home.proof.body: Nothing below changes when you switch products: not a prop, not a class, not a component. Only the theme — and it repaints this page, not a preview box. Switch it right here, or from the panel at the bottom right.
home.proof.title: Same markup. Different product.
home.reach.body: Every other library stops at an accent colour and a radius. Nebula's contract covers seven axes, and the panel at the bottom right drives all of them on this page: product, scheme, corners, density, typeface, motion and glass. Nothing here is re-implemented per product.

reserved.form: The field contract: every input takes a `field` prop and connects to form-atoms through `useFieldProps`, without the core depending on it.
reserved.hooks: The cross-platform hooks of @stellaria/nebula-hooks: theme, media queries, permissions, overlays and motion, with the same API on web and native.
reserved.native: The React Native catalogue. The contract is shared with web — same tokens, same component API — and only the visual layer changes.
reserved.theme: The Theme Creator: build a NebulaTheme, check it against WCAG AA and take the JSON with you. The contract it edits is already closed in docs/02.
reserved.themingStyles: How the NebulaTheme contract reaches every component, and the 128 style props that ride on top of it. Both are already closed in docs/02 and ADR-103 — this section is the reading version.
